title: UWA gets quantum computing access in Quantinuum tie-up
source_used: PR Newswire (Quantinuum press release of 5 Oct 2026); Business News (WA) first sentence only
key_facts: Quantinuum, a US quantum computing company based in Broomfield, Colorado, announced on 5 Oct 2026 that it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with The University of Western Australia (UWA).
UWA-affiliated researchers, students and entrepreneurs will gain cloud-based access to Quantinuum's full-stack quantum computing platform, including Helios, its latest-generation quantum computer.
The two will also explore a university-wide quantum computing applications centre to develop uses in critical minerals, energy, agriculture and healthcare.
Quantinuum programmes such as Q-Net and its Startup Partner Program would offer training and links to a wider quantum community.
The release's own risk statement says the MOU is non-binding, the parties may not enter definitive agreements, and the proposed centre may not be established.
No funding amount, start date or number of users is given.
Quoted: Marvin Lee (Quantinuum country leader), Jingbo Wang (director of UWA's Research Centre for Quantum Information, Simulation and Algorithm) and Petra Andrén (CEO of Quantum Australia).
Business News (WA), 5 Oct 2026: WA enterprises across mining, energy and agriculture could soon tap next-generation computing power following the agreement; paywalled beyond that sentence.
quote_evidence: Through the collaboration, UWA-affiliated researchers, students, and entrepreneurs will gain cloud-based access to Quantinuum's full-stack quantum computing platform, including Helios, the company's latest-generation quantum computer.

The organisations will also explore opportunities to expand UWA's Quantum and AI research ecosystem through a university-wide quantum computing applications centre that would bring together academic, industry, and government stakeholders to identify and develop high-value use cases in critical sectors for Australia's economy, including critical minerals, energy, agriculture, and healthcare.
the Memorandum of Understanding is non-binding, and the parties may not enter into definitive agreements or carry out the activities described; the proposed applications centre may not be established
why_it_matters_hint: Gives a university's researchers cloud access to a leading quantum computer as Australia builds quantum skills, but the memorandum is non-binding.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 (press release 11:00 UTC; Business News WA 03:00 UTC).
notes: The pool item (InnovationAus, 6 Oct 2026) returned HTTP 403, so the original Quantinuum press release was read on PR Newswire. Business News (WA) carried the story first on 5 Oct but is paywalled after its first sentence; Quantum Zeitgeist, Quantum Computing Report and The Quantum Insider also carried the release. The release's claim that Helios is 'the world's most accurate commercial quantum computer' is the company's own and was left out. Not carried in the previous 14 Full Reports (5 Oct carried a different Quantinuum story, its US scale-up funding).
